strings.q-order-mcq.why.venus: Venus is the second planet. It only seems closest because it is the brightest planet in our sky and Earth’s nearest neighbour.
strings.q-order-mcq.why.earth: Earth is the third planet, not the first.
strings.q-order-mcq.why.mars: Mars is the fourth planet. It lies beyond Earth, so it is farther from the Sun than we are.
strings.q-order-mcq.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
strings.q-order-mcq.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun. The order is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
strings.q-order-mcq.dyk: Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system.
strings.q-order-seq.prompt: Put the planets in order, starting with the one nearest the Sun.
strings.q-order-seq.explanation: From the Sun outwards: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
strings.q-order-seq.dyk: Neptune was found with mathematics before anyone saw it: astronomers calculated where it had to be.
strings.q-order-hotspot.why.sun: The Sun is a star, not a planet.
strings.q-order-hotspot.prompt: Find the third planet from the Sun and click it.
strings.q-order-hotspot.explanation: Earth is the third planet, between Venus and Mars. (The picture is not to scale.)
strings.q-order-hotspot.dyk: Earth is the only place we know of that has life.
strings.q-order-card.prompt: Which planet is fourth from the Sun?
strings.q-order-card.explanation: Mars is the fourth planet, right after Earth.
strings.q-planets-ws.prompt: Find the names of the eight planets in the grid.
strings.q-planets-ws.explanation: The eight planets, from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
strings.q-sun-mcq.why.planet: A planet circles a star and does not make its own light. The Sun is the star that all the planets circle.
strings.q-sun-mcq.opt.fire: A huge ball of burning fire
strings.q-sun-mcq.why.fire: Fire needs oxygen, and space has none. The Sun shines because in its core hydrogen is fused into helium, which releases huge amounts of energy.
strings.q-sun-mcq.why.comet: Comets are small balls of ice and dust, a few kilometres wide. The Sun is about 1.4 million kilometres wide.
strings.q-sun-mcq.explanation: The Sun is a star: a giant ball of hot, glowing gas that gives the planets light and warmth.
strings.q-sun-mcq.dyk: The surface of the Sun is about 5,500 °C.
strings.q-sun-tf.why: Half is far too little. The Sun holds about 99.8 %, so all the planets together make up only about 0.2 %.
strings.q-sun-tf.prompt: The Sun holds about half of all the mass in the solar system.
strings.q-sun-tf.explanation: The Sun holds about 99.8 % of the mass of the solar system. Jupiter alone has most of the rest.
strings.q-sun-tf.dyk: About 1.3 million Earths would fit inside the Sun.
strings.q-sun-cloze.text: Light from the Sun takes about {{1}} minutes to reach Earth.
strings.q-sun-cloze.explanation: Sunlight travels about 150 million kilometres to Earth, and the trip takes about 8 minutes.
strings.q-sun-cloze.dyk: We see the Sun as it was about eight minutes ago.
strings.q-sun-beeps.transcript: Eight short beeps, one for each minute of the light’s journey.
strings.q-sun-beeps.why.a: That would be four beeps. Play the sound again and count each one.
strings.q-sun-beeps.why.c: That would be twelve beeps. Count again: there are fewer.
strings.q-sun-beeps.prompt: Each beep stands for one minute of the Sun’s light travelling to Earth. Count the beeps: how long does the light travel?
strings.q-sun-beeps.explanation: You heard eight beeps, so the light takes about 8 minutes. (The sound is a plain test tone, not speech.)
strings.q-sun-beeps.dyk: Light from the Moon reaches us in about 1.3 seconds.
strings.q-types-sort.why.mercury: A small world of rock and metal with a solid surface.
strings.q-types-sort.why.venus: It has a solid, rocky surface under its thick clouds.
strings.q-types-sort.why.earth: Its surface is solid rock with oceans on top.
strings.q-types-sort.why.mars: A cold rocky world with a thin atmosphere.
strings.q-types-sort.why.jupiter: Made mostly of hydrogen and helium, with no solid surface.
strings.q-types-sort.why.saturn: Made mostly of hydrogen and helium, like Jupiter.
strings.q-types-sort.why.uranus: Mostly water, ammonia and methane “ices” around a small rocky core.
strings.q-types-sort.why.neptune: An ice giant like Uranus, with even stronger winds.
strings.q-types-sort.prompt: Sort each planet into its group.
strings.q-types-sort.explanation: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are rocky. Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants. Uranus and Neptune are ice giants.
strings.q-types-sort.dyk: Saturn is so light for its size that it would float on water, if you had a bathtub big enough.
strings.q-types-mcq.why.neptune: Neptune is an ice giant: it holds more heavy “ices” (water, ammonia, methane) than hydrogen and helium.
strings.q-types-mcq.why.mars: Mars is a small rocky planet with a solid surface.
strings.q-types-mcq.why.venus: Venus is rocky too: its thick clouds hide a solid surface.
strings.q-types-mcq.prompt: Which of these planets is a gas giant?
strings.q-types-mcq.explanation: Jupiter and Saturn are the gas giants: they are made mostly of hydrogen and helium.
strings.q-venus-mcq.why.mercury: Mercury is closest to the Sun, but it has almost no atmosphere to hold the heat. Its nights drop to about -180 °C.
strings.q-venus-mcq.why.mars: Mars is cold: it is farther from the Sun than Earth and its air is very thin.
strings.q-venus-mcq.why.jupiter: Jupiter is far from the Sun and its cloud tops are very cold.
strings.q-venus-mcq.prompt: Which planet has the hottest surface in the solar system?
strings.q-venus-mcq.explanation: Venus is the hottest planet. Its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, so the surface is about 467 °C, hot enough to melt lead.
strings.q-venus-mcq.dyk: A day on Venus (243 Earth days) is longer than its year (225 Earth days).
strings.q-venus-cloze.text: Venus is hotter than Mercury because its thick {{1}} traps heat.
strings.q-venus-cloze.prompt: Pick the word that fills the gap.
strings.q-venus-cloze.explanation: Carbon dioxide in Venus’s thick atmosphere traps the Sun’s heat, a very strong greenhouse effect.
strings.q-venus-cloze.dyk: Venus spins backwards compared with most planets.
strings.q-venus-tf.why: Distance is not everything: heat also depends on the atmosphere. Mercury has almost none to hold the heat.
strings.q-venus-tf.prompt: Mercury, the planet closest to the Sun, is the hottest planet.
strings.q-venus-tf.explanation: Venus is hotter. Mercury’s day side reaches about 430 °C but its nights fall to about -180 °C, while Venus stays around 467 °C day and night.
strings.q-giants-multi.opt.rings: Its rings are made of chunks of ice and rock.
strings.q-giants-multi.opt.dense: It is less dense than water.
strings.q-giants-multi.opt.solid: It has a solid surface you could stand on.
strings.q-giants-multi.why.solid: Saturn is a gas giant: you would sink through layers of gas and liquid, with no ground to stand on.
strings.q-giants-multi.why.moons: Saturn has more than 100 moons, and Titan is the largest.
strings.q-giants-multi.prompt: Select the TRUE statements about Saturn.
strings.q-giants-multi.explanation: Saturn’s rings are billions of chunks of ice and rock, and Saturn is the only planet less dense than water. It is a gas giant with no solid surface and has more than 100 moons.
strings.q-giants-typed.prompt: Type the name of the largest planet in the solar system.
strings.q-giants-typed.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet: it has more than twice the mass of all the other planets put together.
strings.q-giants-typed.dyk: Jupiter’s Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth that people have watched for more than 300 years.
strings.q-giants-hotspot.why.jupiter: Jupiter has rings too, but they are faint and very hard to see.
strings.q-giants-hotspot.why.uranus: Uranus has rings, but they are thin and dark.
strings.q-giants-hotspot.prompt: Click the planet with the big, bright rings.
strings.q-giants-hotspot.explanation: Saturn’s rings are the biggest and brightest of any planet.
strings.q-giants-hotspot.dyk: All four giant planets have rings, but Saturn’s are by far the most spectacular.
strings.q-facts-match.r.mars: The Red Planet, red from rusty dust
strings.q-facts-match.prompt: Match each planet with the fact it is best known for.
strings.q-facts-match.explanation: Mars is red because iron minerals in its dust rust. Venus is the hottest, Jupiter the largest, Saturn has the brightest rings, Uranus spins on its side and Neptune has the fastest winds.
strings.q-facts-match.dyk: Neptune’s winds blow at more than 2,000 km/h, faster than the speed of sound on Earth.
strings.q-facts-cross.clue.uranus: The planet that spins on its side
strings.q-facts-cross.clue.neptune: The windiest planet, farthest from the Sun
strings.q-facts-cross.prompt: Solve the crossword: every answer is a planet.
strings.q-facts-cross.explanation: Every answer is the name of a planet.
strings.q-facts-cross.dyk: Uranus was the first planet found with a telescope, in 1781.
strings.q-moons-match.r.europa: An ice shell over a hidden ocean
strings.q-moons-match.r.ganymede: The largest moon, bigger than Mercury
strings.q-moons-match.prompt: Match each moon with what it is known for.
strings.q-moons-match.explanation: Titan has a thick atmosphere, Europa has an ocean under its ice, Io has hundreds of volcanoes and Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system.
strings.q-moons-match.dyk: Under its ice, Europa very likely has a saltwater ocean, one of the best places to look for life beyond Earth.
strings.q-moons-typed.prompt: Type the name of Earth’s only natural satellite.
strings.q-moons-typed.explanation: Earth has one natural satellite: the Moon, about 384,000 kilometres away.
strings.q-moons-typed.dyk: The Moon moves about 3.8 cm farther from Earth every year.
strings.q-moons-mcq.why.venus: Venus has no moons at all.
strings.q-moons-mcq.why.earth: Earth has just one moon, the Moon.
strings.q-moons-mcq.why.neptune: Neptune has many moons, and its largest is Triton.
strings.q-moons-mcq.prompt: Which planet has two small moons called Phobos and Deimos?
strings.q-moons-mcq.explanation: Mars has two tiny moons, Phobos and Deimos, which may be captured asteroids.
strings.q-moons-mcq.dyk: Phobos gets closer to Mars every year and will break up in tens of millions of years.
strings.q-moons-card.back: The largest moon in the solar system. It orbits Jupiter.
strings.q-moons-card.explanation: Ganymede is bigger than the planet Mercury.
strings.q-moons-card.dyk: Ganymede is the only moon known to have its own magnetic field.
strings.q-beyond-mcq.why.planet: Pluto was called the ninth planet until 2006, when astronomers defined a planet as a world that has also cleared its orbit of other objects. Pluto has not.
strings.q-beyond-mcq.why.asteroid: Pluto is far larger than a typical asteroid: it is round and has five moons.
strings.q-beyond-mcq.why.moon: Pluto orbits the Sun on its own path, not Neptune.
strings.q-beyond-mcq.prompt: How do astronomers classify Pluto today?
strings.q-beyond-mcq.explanation: In 2006 the International Astronomical Union classified Pluto as a dwarf planet. It lives in the Kuiper belt, beyond Neptune.
strings.q-beyond-mcq.dyk: The New Horizons probe flew past Pluto in 2015 and found a heart-shaped bright region on it.
strings.q-beyond-order.prompt: Put these in order, starting with the one nearest the Sun.
strings.q-beyond-order.explanation: From the Sun: Mars, the asteroid belt, Jupiter, Neptune, then the Kuiper belt beyond Neptune.
strings.q-beyond-order.dyk: The asteroid belt is mostly empty space: spacecraft pass through it without trouble.
strings.q-beyond-cloze.text: Most asteroids orbit the Sun in a belt between Mars and {{1}}.
strings.q-beyond-cloze.explanation: The main asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
strings.q-explore-timeline.sputnik: Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, is launched
strings.q-explore-timeline.apollo: Apollo 11 lands the first people on the Moon
strings.q-explore-timeline.voyager: Voyager 2 is launched on its tour of the giant planets
strings.q-explore-timeline.prompt: Put these milestones in order, oldest first.
strings.q-explore-timeline.explanation: Sputnik 1 flew in 1957, Apollo 11 landed on the Moon in 1969, Voyager 2 was launched in 1977 and New Horizons flew past Pluto in 2015.
strings.q-explore-timeline.dyk: Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft that has visited Uranus and Neptune.
strings.q-explore-mcq.why.voyager: Voyager 2 visited Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, but not Pluto.
strings.q-explore-mcq.why.apollo: Apollo 11 went to the Moon, not to Pluto.
strings.q-explore-mcq.prompt: Which mission flew past Pluto in 2015?
strings.q-explore-mcq.explanation: New Horizons flew past Pluto on 14 July 2015, after a journey of more than nine years.
strings.q-explore-mcq.dyk: New Horizons took more than nine years to reach Pluto.
strings.ss.unit.sun.title: The Sun and the planets
strings.ss.unit.sun.summary: Meet our star and the eight planets that circle it.
strings.ss.unit.types.title: Rocky and giant planets
strings.ss.unit.types.summary: Why the inner planets are solid and the outer ones are huge.
strings.ss.unit.moons.title: Moons and beyond
strings.ss.unit.moons.summary: Moons, asteroids, dwarf planets and how we explored them.
strings.ss.fact.f-eight-planets: The solar system has eight planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, in that order from the Sun.
strings.ss.fact.f-planet-types: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are rocky planets, Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants and Uranus and Neptune are ice giants.
strings.ss.fact.f-sun-star: The Sun is a star: a giant ball of hot, glowing gas whose surface is about 5,500 °C.
strings.ss.fact.f-sun-mass: The Sun holds about 99.8 % of the mass of the solar system.
strings.ss.fact.f-light-time: Light from the Sun takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.
strings.ss.fact.f-venus-hot: Venus is the hottest planet, with a surface about 467 °C, because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat.
strings.ss.fact.f-mercury-night: Mercury has almost no atmosphere, so its nights fall to about -180 °C.
strings.ss.fact.f-mars-red: Mars is called the Red Planet because iron minerals in its dust rust.
strings.ss.fact.f-mars-moons: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, that may be captured asteroids.
strings.ss.fact.f-jupiter-mass: Jupiter is the largest planet, with more than twice the combined mass of all the other planets.
strings.ss.fact.f-saturn: Saturn is the only planet less dense than water, and its rings are billions of chunks of ice and rock.
strings.ss.fact.f-neptune-winds: Neptune has winds of more than 2,000 kilometres per hour.
strings.ss.fact.f-ganymede: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is the largest moon in the solar system and bigger than Mercury.
strings.ss.fact.f-titan: Titan, a moon of Saturn, is the only moon with a thick atmosphere.
strings.ss.fact.f-europa: Europa, a moon of Jupiter, very likely has a saltwater ocean under its ice.
strings.ss.fact.f-io: Io, a moon of Jupiter, is the most volcanically active world in the solar system.
strings.ss.fact.f-pluto: Pluto is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt.
strings.ss.fact.f-asteroid-belt: Most asteroids orbit the Sun in the main belt between Mars and Jupiter.
strings.ss.fact.f-kuiper: The Kuiper belt is a region of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
strings.ss.fact.f-sputnik: Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, was launched in 1957.
strings.ss.fact.f-apollo-11: Apollo 11 landed the first people on the Moon in 1969.
strings.ss.fact.f-voyager-2: Voyager 2 was launched in 1977 and is the only spacecraft that has visited Uranus and Neptune.
strings.ss.fact.f-new-horizons: New Horizons flew past Pluto in July 2015.

strings.ss.obj.obj-sun: Explain what the Sun is and why it matters to the planets.
strings.ss.obj.obj-planet-types: Sort the planets into rocky planets, gas giants and ice giants.
strings.ss.obj.obj-venus-hot: Explain why Venus is the hottest planet.
strings.ss.obj.obj-giants: Recall key facts about Jupiter and Saturn.

strings.ss.obj.obj-beyond: Describe what lies beyond the planets: asteroids, the Kuiper belt and dwarf planets.

strings.ss.art.sun.title: The Sun
strings.ss.art.sun.body: The Sun is a star, a giant ball of hot, glowing gas. It holds about 99.8 % of the mass of the solar system, and its surface is about 5,500 °C. Its light takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.
strings.ss.art.rocky.title: The rocky planets
strings.ss.art.rocky.body: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are small, rocky worlds with solid surfaces. Venus is the hottest planet because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, while Mercury, with almost no atmosphere, cools to about -180 °C at night. Mars looks red because iron minerals in its dust rust.
strings.ss.art.giants.title: The giant planets
strings.ss.art.giants.body: Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants, made mostly of hydrogen and helium. Jupiter has more than twice the mass of all the other planets together. Saturn is the only planet less dense than water and has bright rings of ice and rock. Uranus and Neptune are ice giants: Uranus spins on its side and Neptune has winds of more than 2,000 kilometres per hour.
strings.ss.art.moons.title: Moons
strings.ss.art.moons.body: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is the largest moon in the solar system and bigger than Mercury. Titan, a moon of Saturn, has a thick atmosphere. Europa very likely hides an ocean under its ice, and Io is the most volcanic world we know. Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.
strings.ss.art.beyond.title: Beyond the planets
strings.ss.art.beyond.body: Most asteroids orbit the Sun in a belt between Mars and Jupiter. Beyond Neptune lies the Kuiper belt, a region of icy bodies where the dwarf planet Pluto lives. The New Horizons probe flew past Pluto in July 2015.
strings.ss.asset.solar.alt: A diagram of the Sun at the far left and the eight planets in a row, not to scale: small Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, then large Jupiter, Saturn with its rings, Uranus and Neptune.
strings.ss.asset.beeps.alt: A plain test tone: eight short, identical beeps. It is not speech.
strings.enc.t.t-galileo: Galileo sees four moons of Jupiter
strings.enc.t.t-galileo.text: Through his telescope Galileo spots Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto circling Jupiter.
strings.enc.t.t-uranus.text: William Herschel spots a new planet beyond Saturn: Uranus, the planet that spins on its side.
strings.enc.t.t-neptune.text: Astronomers find Neptune, the planet of the fastest winds, almost exactly where calculation said it would be.
strings.enc.t.t-pluto.text: Clyde Tombaugh finds Pluto. For 76 years it is called the ninth planet.
strings.enc.t.t-sputnik.text: Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, is launched.
strings.enc.t.t-apollo.text: Apollo 11 lands the first people on the Moon.
strings.enc.t.t-voyager.text: Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft that has visited Uranus and Neptune.
strings.enc.t.t-horizons.text: New Horizons flies past Pluto in July 2015.
strings.enc.h.h-sun.title: The home star
strings.enc.h.h-sun.intro: Everything begins with the Sun. Follow the clues, read the pages and collect what they hold.
strings.enc.h.h-sun.s-sun-star.clue: I am the heart of the family: a ball of hot, glowing gas that holds almost all of its mass. Find my page.
strings.enc.h.h-sun.s-sun-star.name: The brass sunburst
strings.enc.h.h-sun.s-sun-mercury.clue: Four small, rocky worlds huddle near the Sun. Find their page and learn which of them stands first in line.
strings.enc.h.h-sun.s-sun-mercury.name: The Mercury token
strings.enc.h.h-sun.s-sun-light.clue: My light is quick, but it still needs time to reach you. Find my page and see how long it travels.
strings.enc.h.h-sun.s-sun-light.name: The brass hourglass
strings.enc.h.h-rocky.title: Worlds of rock and gas
strings.enc.h.h-rocky.intro: Rock, gas and ice: find the pages and learn what each world is made of.
strings.enc.h.h-rocky.s-rocky-venus.clue: One world wears a blanket of thick air and is the hottest of all. Find the page of the rocky planets.
strings.enc.h.h-rocky.s-rocky-venus.name: The brass lantern
strings.enc.h.h-rocky.s-rocky-gas.clue: Two giants are made mostly of hydrogen and helium. Find the page of the giant planets.
strings.enc.h.h-rocky.s-rocky-gas.name: The gas flask
strings.enc.h.h-rocky.s-rocky-rings.clue: One planet wears the brightest rings of all. Find its page and see which one it is.
strings.enc.h.h-rocky.s-rocky-rings.name: The brass ring
strings.enc.h.h-moons.title: Moons and the far dark
strings.enc.h.h-moons.intro: Moons, belts and tiny frozen worlds: the last pages of the book.
strings.enc.h.h-moons.s-moons-mars.clue: A red world keeps two tiny moons that may be captured asteroids. Find the page of the moons.
strings.enc.h.h-moons.s-moons-mars.name: The little brass moon
strings.enc.h.h-moons.s-moons-pluto.clue: Past Neptune a belt of icy bodies circles in the dark. Find the page about what lies beyond the planets.
strings.enc.h.h-moons.s-moons-pluto.name: The icy compass
strings.enc.h.h-moons.s-moons-horizons.clue: A small probe crossed the dark for nine years to visit a tiny world. Find its page.
strings.enc.h.h-moons.s-moons-horizons.name: The brass probe
strings.maze.w.w-sun.desc: The observatory wing: the Sun, and the eight planets in order.
strings.maze.r.sun-hall.desc: A round hall under a copper dome. Brass instruments tick in the dark.
strings.maze.c.sun-hall.name: The astronomer
strings.maze.c.sun-hall.line: Welcome! Count outwards from the Sun: eight planets circle it, and not one of them makes its own light.
strings.maze.c.sun-hall.hint: Count outwards from the Sun: Mercury comes first, Neptune last.
strings.maze.c.sun-hall.wrong: Not quite. Count again from the Sun outwards.
strings.maze.r.sun-orrery.desc: A brass model of the planets turns slowly on its arms.
strings.maze.c.sun-orrery.name: The clockmaker
strings.maze.c.sun-orrery.line: My orrery turns every planet around the Sun. Earth is the third ring, and it is the only world we know of that has life.
strings.maze.c.sun-orrery.hint: In the orrery Mars sits right after Earth, and Venus right before it.
strings.maze.c.sun-orrery.wrong: A gear slipped. Look at the rings again.
strings.maze.r.sun-corona.desc: Golden light pours through a lens as tall as a door.
strings.maze.c.sun-corona.name: The solar physicist
strings.maze.c.sun-corona.line: The Sun is a star: a giant ball of hot, glowing gas. Its surface is about 5,500 °C.
strings.maze.c.sun-corona.hint: Fire needs oxygen and space has none, so the Sun is not burning. In its core hydrogen is fused into helium.
strings.maze.c.sun-corona.wrong: Too dim. Think about what makes the Sun shine.
strings.maze.r.sun-library.desc: Shelves of star charts reach up into the shadows.
strings.maze.c.sun-library.name: The librarian
strings.maze.c.sun-library.line: About 99.8 % of all the mass in the solar system is in the Sun. All the planets together make up only about 0.2 %.
strings.maze.c.sun-library.hint: The Sun holds nearly all of the mass: far more than half.
strings.maze.r.sun-dome.desc: The dome opens on a bright sky. A long line of beeps counts the light on its way.
strings.maze.c.sun-dome.name: The light keeper
strings.maze.c.sun-dome.line: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. Light from the Moon needs only about 1.3 seconds.
strings.maze.c.sun-dome.hint: Eight minutes: one beep for each minute of the journey.
strings.maze.c.sun-dome.wrong: The light was faster than that. Listen again.
strings.maze.r.sun-key.desc: The key of the wing hangs in the focus of the great lens.
strings.maze.c.sun-key.name: The keeper of the key
strings.maze.c.sun-key.line: You walked the whole wing. Take the key: the planets are no stranger to you now.
strings.maze.c.sun-key.hint: Take the key to see how well you did.
strings.maze.c.sun-key.wrong: Take the key anyway. You can walk the wing again.
strings.maze.w.w-worlds.desc: The forge wing: solid worlds, hot worlds and the giants.
strings.maze.r.worlds-hall.desc: Anvils and globes of stone stand in rows. The air smells of hot metal.
strings.maze.c.worlds-hall.name: The geologist
strings.maze.c.worlds-hall.line: The four inner planets are rocky: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars. Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants, Uranus and Neptune ice giants.
strings.maze.c.worlds-hall.hint: A rocky planet has a solid surface. A giant is made mostly of gas or ices.
strings.maze.c.worlds-hall.wrong: That cracked. Think about what each planet is made of.
strings.maze.r.worlds-types.desc: Three great bins stand under three banners: rock, gas and ice.
strings.maze.c.worlds-types.name: The sorter
strings.maze.c.worlds-types.line: Jupiter and Saturn are made mostly of hydrogen and helium. Uranus and Neptune hold more heavy ices of water, ammonia and methane.
strings.maze.c.worlds-types.hint: Gas giants: hydrogen and helium. Ice giants: water, ammonia and methane.
strings.maze.c.worlds-types.wrong: Wrong bin. Check the planet again.
strings.maze.r.worlds-furnace.desc: The walls glow orange. Even the air presses on you like a blanket.
strings.maze.c.worlds-furnace.name: The probe engineer
strings.maze.c.worlds-furnace.line: Venus is the hottest planet: its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat. The surface is about 467 °C, hot enough to melt lead.
strings.maze.c.worlds-furnace.hint: It is not only about distance: Mercury is closer but has almost no atmosphere to hold the heat.
strings.maze.c.worlds-furnace.wrong: That one cooled off. Think about the atmosphere.
strings.maze.r.worlds-giants.desc: Great paintings of swirling clouds, and one huge red eye.
strings.maze.c.worlds-giants.name: The storm watcher
strings.maze.c.worlds-giants.line: Jupiter is the largest planet. Its Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth that people have watched for more than 300 years.
strings.maze.c.worlds-giants.hint: The largest planet is Jupiter. The planet with the brightest rings is Saturn.
strings.maze.c.worlds-giants.wrong: A storm of a mistake. Look again.
strings.maze.r.worlds-vault.desc: Every planet has a drawer here, with one fact kept inside.
strings.maze.c.worlds-vault.name: The curator
strings.maze.c.worlds-vault.line: Mars is red because iron in its dust rusts. Uranus spins on its side and Neptune has the fastest winds, over 2,000 km/h.
strings.maze.c.worlds-vault.hint: Match each planet with what it is famous for: red, hot, largest, rings, sideways, windy.
strings.maze.c.worlds-vault.right: The drawer slides shut with a click.
strings.maze.r.worlds-key.desc: A heavy iron key lies on a pedestal of cooled lava.
strings.maze.c.worlds-key.name: The forge master
strings.maze.c.worlds-key.line: You have crossed the forge. Take the key: you know the rocky worlds from the giants now.
strings.maze.c.worlds-key.hint: Take the key to see how well you did.
strings.maze.c.worlds-key.wrong: Take it anyway, and walk the wing again if you wish.
strings.maze.w.w-beyond.desc: The tower wing: moons, the belt of asteroids, Pluto and the missions that reached them.
strings.maze.r.beyond-hall.desc: Silver light falls through a tall round window.
strings.maze.c.beyond-hall.name: The moon watcher
strings.maze.c.beyond-hall.line: The Moon is Earth’s only natural satellite, about 384,000 kilometres away. It drifts about 3.8 cm farther every year.
strings.maze.c.beyond-hall.hint: Earth has one Moon. Mars has two tiny ones, Phobos and Deimos.
strings.maze.c.beyond-hall.wrong: Not this time. The Moon is closer than you think.
strings.maze.r.beyond-moons.desc: Four glowing globes float over the beds: orange, icy, yellow and grey.
strings.maze.c.beyond-moons.name: The moon gardener
strings.maze.c.beyond-moons.line: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is bigger than Mercury. Titan has a thick orange atmosphere, Europa an ocean under its ice, and Io hundreds of volcanoes.
strings.maze.c.beyond-moons.hint: Titan: atmosphere. Europa: ocean. Io: volcanoes. Ganymede: the largest moon.
strings.maze.r.beyond-belt.desc: A glass bridge leads through a field of drifting rocks.
strings.maze.c.beyond-belt.name: The asteroid pilot
strings.maze.c.beyond-belt.line: Most asteroids orbit the Sun between Mars and Jupiter. The belt is mostly empty space, so spacecraft pass through it without trouble.
strings.maze.c.beyond-belt.hint: From the Sun: Mars, the asteroid belt, Jupiter, Neptune, then the Kuiper belt.
strings.maze.c.beyond-belt.wrong: Bump! Steer back and look at the order again.
strings.maze.r.beyond-control.desc: Screens glow along the wall. A clock counts the years since the first flight.
strings.maze.c.beyond-control.name: The mission controller
strings.maze.c.beyond-control.line: Sputnik 1 flew in 1957, Apollo 11 landed on the Moon in 1969, Voyager 2 launched in 1977 and New Horizons flew past Pluto in 2015.
strings.maze.c.beyond-control.wrong: We have a problem. Check the dates again.
strings.maze.r.beyond-edge.desc: A cold balcony looks out on the dark. Far below, a small icy world glints.
strings.maze.c.beyond-edge.name: The cartographer
strings.maze.c.beyond-edge.line: Pluto lives in the Kuiper belt beyond Neptune. In 2006 astronomers classified it as a dwarf planet. New Horizons found a heart-shaped bright region on it.
strings.maze.c.beyond-edge.hint: Pluto is a dwarf planet, not one of the eight planets.
strings.maze.r.beyond-key.desc: The key hangs among the stars of a painted ceiling.
strings.maze.c.beyond-key.name: The tower keeper
strings.maze.c.beyond-key.line: You have gone beyond the planets. Take the key: the whole solar system is at your feet.
strings.maze.c.beyond-key.hint: Take the key to see how well you did.
strings.maze.c.beyond-key.wrong: Take it anyway, and fly the wing again if you wish.
strings.maze.throne: The throne room of the stars
strings.maze.throne.desc: Three keys open the golden doors. A last gauntlet of questions from every wing waits before the throne: win one star and the crown is yours.
strings.rpg.story.1: In the old observatory on the hill, the orrery, a brass model of the solar system, has stopped. Its planets hang crooked and the Sun at its centre has gone dark.
strings.rpg.story.2: You are Nova, the new keeper of the observatory. To start the orrery again you must set every part right, using only what is true about the real solar system.
strings.rpg.story.3: But muddled ideas, old myths about the planets, have crept into three halls: the Sun's court, the rocky road and the giants' sea, and the icy moons. Beat each myth with a fact.
strings.rpg.story.end: The last myth falls and the orrery begins to turn. Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, the giants and their moons: every part runs true, because you set it right with what you learned.
strings.rpg.a.rocky: The Rocky Road and the Giants' Sea
strings.rpg.n.vela.1: Welcome, Nova. The Sun is not a planet: it is a star, a giant ball of hot, glowing gas that gives the planets light and warmth.
strings.rpg.n.vela.2: Eight planets circle it. From the Sun outwards: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
strings.rpg.n.vela.3: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. Beat the myths in this court, then the Corona Guardian, and the gate will open.
strings.rpg.n.rho.1: The four inner planets are small and rocky: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars. Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants, Uranus and Neptune are ice giants.
strings.rpg.n.rho.2: Many people think Mercury is the hottest planet because it is closest to the Sun. It is not: Venus is hotter, because its thick carbon dioxide air traps the heat.
strings.rpg.n.rho.3: Jupiter is the largest planet and Saturn has the brightest rings. Face the myths that guard the road and the giants' sea.
strings.rpg.n.lamp.1: I light the lamps along this road every night. The bright dot we call the evening star is really Venus: its clouds reflect sunlight very well.
strings.rpg.n.lamp.2: Saturn is so light for its size that it would float on water, if you had a bathtub big enough.
strings.rpg.n.luna.1: Earth has one moon, about 384,000 kilometres away. Mars has two tiny ones, Phobos and Deimos.
strings.rpg.n.luna.2: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is the largest moon in the solar system and is bigger than Mercury. Europa very likely hides a salty ocean under its ice.
strings.rpg.n.luna.3: In 2006 Pluto was classified as a dwarf planet. Beyond Neptune lies the Kuiper belt. Win this last hall and the orrery will turn.
